sections.h2: The city approval step before a West Chicago sale
sections.html:
A West Chicago sale has one local step that most Illinois suburbs lack: the city must approve the structure before any deed is recorded. The same paperwork applies to a listed sale, a private deal or a buyer paying cash for a property in any condition. Plan for it early, because the inspection is valid for six months and the city asks for scheduling at least two months before closing.

The city sits on the western edge of DuPage County, about 32 miles from downtown Chicago, with Illinois Route 59 running north and south and Routes 38 and 64 running east and west. Buyers who commute use the Metra station on Main Street or drive to I-88 and I-355, so mention both in your listing.

The Community Development Department inspects the structure for basic maintenance and life safety, and no Deed Certification Number is issued without an approved inspection unless an exemption applies. A visit takes about 30 minutes and happens Monday through Friday between 9 a.m. and 3 p.m. Vacant lots are inspected too.

  • Smoke detectors must be present and working.
  • Ground fault interrupters must be installed where the checklist calls for them.
  • Stair railings must meet the minimum standard.
  • The structure must show adequate property maintenance, and vacant parcels are checked for tall grass, weeds and garbage.

The fee is a $100.00 base charge plus $0.12 per square foot, using the square footage the township supplies to the city. A vacant parcel adds a flat $20.00. If the house fails, you can fix the items and request a re-inspection at no added charge, or sell as-is and leave the repairs to the buyer.

sections.h2: Seller steps before the deed records
sections.html:
The city lays the steps out in order, and skipping one stalls the recording.

Seller steps from the City of West Chicago Property Transactions page
OrderStepFee or timing
1City inspection$100.00 base plus $0.12 per square foot; valid six months
2Final water and sewer readingCall Finance at least 2 working days before closing
3Clear city balancesInspection fees, water bills, parking tickets, ordinance violations, liens, waste services
4Deed Certification NumberForm signed by a seller or agent, presented at 475 Main Street

The number must be attached to the deed when the title is recorded. Payment at City Hall can be made by cash, check, or debit or credit card.

Certain transfers skip the inspection fee but still need a certification number. They include new construction, deeds that secure or release a debt, corrective deeds with no added consideration, and a sale where the occupant does not change. A final water reading is still required for those exempt deeds, and the city takes up to five business days to decide an exemption.

When a seller declines to repair failed items, the buyer signs a Letter of Intent Agreement and posts a $1,600.00 bond with the Community Development Department. The buyer then has 90 days to finish repairs and pass an inspection, and one free 90-day extension is available if requested in person before the deadline. After an approved inspection the city refunds $1,500.00 within two to three weeks, because it keeps a $100.00 administrative fee.

This rule shapes cash offers on rough houses. A buyer who plans renovations can still close, but the bond and the 90-day clock are part of the buyer's cost, so ask any purchaser how they handle the city's requirements before you sign.

West Chicago is a young, family-heavy market. Owners live in 70.9% of homes, typical values sit at $336,800, rent is $1,469 a month and household income is $99,927. Population is estimated at 25,296 for July 2025, down 1.3% from the 2020 base of 25,614, and 92.2% of residents stayed at one address over the prior year, a sign of low turnover.

Median monthly owner costs run $2,428 with a mortgage and $1,035 without one. Buyers with a monthly budget in mind will compare those numbers with your asking price.

sections.h2: Property tax and the closing statement
sections.html:
West Chicago is in DuPage County, which bills property tax a year behind. Recent bills were mailed in late April, with installments on June 1 and September 1, so confirm the current dates with the county treasurer. The treasurer's page lists the general homestead exemption and the senior exemption at $8,000 each, so check your bill for both. If a mortgage servicer pays your tax, a yellow box on the bill says so and you should not pay twice.

The title company splits the unpaid tax between seller and buyer on the settlement statement, and the state taxes the transfer itself at a half dollar per $500 of declared value. Ask the DuPage County recorder what the county adds. Illinois also requires a seller of one to four units to deliver a finished disclosure report ahead of contract signing (765 ILCS 77/20).

West Chicago requires a Rental Property License for residential landlords and annual rental inspections tied to the International Property Maintenance Code standard. If you are selling a rental, confirm that your license and inspection record are current, because open city items surface at the same Community Development counter that handles the sale inspection. A sale where the occupant or tenant does not change can qualify for the inspection fee exemption, so bring the signed deed to the Director of Community Development and ask for a ruling before closing.

Book the inspection first, since the city wants about two months of lead time and the result lasts six months. While you wait, pull your payoff figure, your tax bill and any permit papers. Call Finance for the final water reading at least 2 working days before closing, and pay any city balances so the Deed Certification Number can be issued.

A cash buyer on a house that fails the inspection can still close, since the buyer takes the as-is route with the bond. Ask them in advance how they plan to handle it. At the table you sign the deed, the title company settles the taxes and payoffs, and the certification number goes on the deed before it is recorded.

faqs.q: Do I need a city inspection to sell my house in West Chicago?
faqs.a: Yes, except for the exempt transfer types the city lists. Without an approved inspection the city issues no Deed Certification Number, and the visit costs $100.00 plus $0.12 per square foot. It stays valid for six months, so schedule it about two months before closing.

faqs.q: Can I sell a West Chicago house that fails the inspection?
faqs.a: Yes. You can repair the items and get a free re-inspection, or sell as-is. With an as-is sale the buyer posts a $1,600.00 bond and has 90 days to finish repairs and pass.

faqs.q: Who schedules the final water reading in West Chicago?
faqs.a: The seller does. Contact the city's Finance Department at least 2 working days before closing, pay the unbilled water and sewer use, and clear any other city balances before the certification number is issued.

faqs.q: Does West Chicago charge a local transfer tax?
faqs.a: The city's published steps include inspection fees and a Deed Certification Number but no local transfer tax rate. The state's share is a half dollar on every $500 declared, and the DuPage County recorder can tell you what the county adds.

faqs.q: When are DuPage County property tax bills due?
faqs.a: Illinois bills a year behind, and recent installments fell on June 1 and September 1. Confirm the current dates with the county treasurer. Your closing statement splits the unpaid portion between seller and buyer.
